rationale: The Justice Department's new charges against former FBI Director James Comey were the day's top US national story (12 US outlets, 9 front pages), unsealed a week before the midterms. Focal. Brazil's Lula winning a fourth term ranked second but is international with only indirect US ties (Trump called the result 'rigged'). Anthropic's IPO filing, Walter Koenig's death and the $1-million voter-fraud reward were noted but are smaller or harder to draw truthfully alongside the focal story. The same-day ruling that Maurene Comey was unlawfully fired is related but a separate case; left out to keep one clear picture. No Boston story matched the national significance.

stories.name: James Comey charged a third time
facts: Federal prosecutors charged former FBI Director James Comey with transmitting national defense information and conspiring to do so, in court papers unsealed Monday.
The case concerns an October 2016 New York Times story about a secret court order for Yahoo to scan emails; prosecutors say Comey had staff talk to the reporter.
The charges were filed as a criminal information, not a grand jury indictment; Comey's lawyers say they are time-barred. It is the third attempt to prosecute him in about a year.
Comey said in a video statement that he is innocent.
